value.answer: Short-term, low doses of melatonin (around 5 mg or less) appear safe for most adults. Side effects are usually mild and go away when you stop, with headache and drowsiness the most common. Long-term safety is less clear. A preliminary AHA study linked 12+ months of use in people with insomnia to a higher chance of heart failure, but it hasn't been peer-reviewed and can't prove cause. A later 2026 analysis found no significant link, though I only saw a summary of it. Supplement strength also varies a lot, and melatonin can interact with blood thinners and antidepressants, so check with a doctor or pharmacist if you take any of those or other medications.
